data.body:
RP-01 candidate-accounting proposal revised after maintained-OSS comparison; no maintainer decision recorded yet. New brief: `.joe-janitor/rp01-request-accounting-prior-art.md`. Current upstream evidence as of 2026-08-16: Pydantic AI (19,335 stars) explicitly treats model fallback as distinct from Agent retry and says retry layers do not share budgets; `RunUsage.requests` remains the `UsageLimits.request_limit` counter, while `FallbackModel` tries candidates inside one outer model request and retains only the winning response. LangChain (144,351 stars) records fallback candidates as child callback runs while standard usage remains token metadata. LiteLLM (56,481 stars) keeps router `total_calls`/`fail_calls`/`success_calls` separate from retry/fallback bounds and spend. OpenAI Agents SDK (28,689 stars) folds physical requests into primary `Usage.requests` only when its model adapter authoritatively owns and preserves those request usage entries.

Revised recommendation: do not add `candidate_requests` to Rebar core usage or JSONL. Keep Pydantic `requests` as the sole request-budget/core usage count; bound fallback fan-out through the explicit candidate chain and predicate; retain disabled/separately bounded provider SDK retries; and record candidate identity plus returned/raised outcome as trace or journal events through public model instrumentation when operational visibility is required. Never synthesize failed-attempt token usage. The prior four-allowlist compatibility probe remains relevant only if the maintainer instead selects a parallel usage-field alternative.
